grh_12ee375781a02ba958e2.title: What It Takes
paragraphs: A January blizzard strands Dr. Christian, Judy and a cross-section of strangers on an interurban bus. Among them are a wounded veteran disgusted by civilian complaining, a prisoner being returned under guard, a struggling musician, and a young mother whose undernourished baby urgently needs milk. Dr. Christian discovers that the mother is also clinging to the belief that her husband will come home, although the military telegram she carries reports him killed. As the stalled bus grows colder, the passengers who had been arguing and thinking only of themselves begin giving up coats, blankets, comfort and safety to protect the mother and child. Men set out through the storm for help, and even the prisoner, given a genuine opportunity to run, chooses not to escape. By morning the crisis has shown each of them what it takes to put another person's life ahead of his own grievances.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on January 2, 1946. It is listed as episode 371 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_1206ae39e09e30f0df66.title: Operation Music Box
paragraphs: In London, Harry meets a woman searching antique dealers for three music boxes purchased during a specific period. He learns that one of them contains a hidden fortune in jewels and steals her list so he can find it first. Harry tracks down the owners, breaking into a collector's flat and destroying music boxes as he searches, only to discover that the crucial third box has already been given away to charity. At an orphan institution he arrives just as officials dedicate a new wing. A child had accidentally dropped the donated box, exposing its secret compartment and jewels; the gems were sold to finance the building. Harry can only listen as the intact music box is played at the ceremony, his hoped-for fortune permanently beyond reach.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on October 5, 1951. It is listed as episode 10 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] and Anton Karas. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director, Harry Alan Towers as producer, and [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] as writer.

grh_121251c78e8d71e73c71.title: Brave Men
paragraphs: A tribute to Ernie Pyle built from dramatized passages of Brave Men rather than one continuous story. The program moves among infantrymen waiting for battle, battlefield deaths, exhausted troops, small moments of tenderness and Pyle's observations about the bond among men living constantly with death. It repeatedly contrasts the reality of casualties with the simplified picture of victory at home, then closes by recalling Pyle's own death on Ie Shima and the soldiers who buried him as one of their own.
